title: Why Arabako Txakolina tastes the way it does

lede.text: A valley in northern Álava with an Atlantic climate. Its txakoli is high in acidity, with a slightly bitter aftertaste.

chapters.title: The Ayala valley
paras: Arabako Txakolina is made in the Ayala valley, in the north of Álava.
The zone covers five municipalities: Amurrio, Artziniega, Ayala/Aiara, Laudio/Llodio and Okondo.
Vineyards are always close to the wineries, within about 3 km.

fly.label: The Ayala valley
fly.caption: Five municipalities in the north of Álava.

chapters.title: Atlantic, with a southern wind
paras: The pliego calls the climate Atlantic. Rain averages 899 litres a year.
From April to October the average light is 12.11 hours a day. The south wind blows on 170 days a year, and it brings air to the leaves.
The average temperature is 13.1 °C. The average high is 18.7 °C and the average low is 7.5 °C.
This microclimate lets the grapes be picked at about 12% potential strength.

fly.label: The Ayala valley
fly.caption: The south wind blows on 170 days a year.

chapters.title: Soils from acid to alkaline
paras: The pliego says little about the soil. The average pH in the vineyards is between 5.2 and 8.2. Active limestone is between 6.2 and 9.2.
It links this to the wine's typical acidity. It also links it to a slightly bitter aftertaste.

chapters.title: Hondarribi Zuri against mildew
paras: The main grapes are Hondarrabi Zuri, Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia (Petit Courbu). Seven other varieties are authorised.
Yields are capped at 13,000 kg of grapes per hectare. The wine yield may not exceed 70 litres per 100 kg of grapes.
The varieties have small, tight bunches with thick skins. They resist mildew, which is a high risk in this wet zone.
The pliego gives total acidity of 9 to 12 g/l as tartaric, volatile acidity under 1 g/l and a pH of about 3.
It describes the wine's acidity as neither too much nor too little, with a slight bitterness and citrus and herbal flavours. The colour runs from green to straw yellow.
